- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially near end of horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply downward correction of 1-3% in next 5-7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion correction starting from day of sentiment pivot.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to recent highs; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0σ above recent 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0 point bias upward for next 5 days.
- Model often ignores sentiment decay after 10–15 days; if sentiment drops below 0.33 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for remaining days.
